title: Safe Work Method Statement for High Risk Construction Work
abstract:
This WorkSafe WA information sheet provides detailed guidance on preparing and implementing Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS) for high-risk construction work. An SWMS is a legal document that sets out the high-risk construction work to be carried out, the hazards and risks arising from that work, and the measures to be put in place to control the risks.

High-risk construction work includes work on or near roads, work near traffic corridors, work at heights above 2 metres, work using powered mobile plant, and work involving excavations. Traffic management and road work activities fall squarely within this definition, making SWMS preparation mandatory.

The guide lists all 19 categories of high-risk construction work, explains the required content of an SWMS, the consultation process with workers, review and revision requirements, and record-keeping obligations. SWMS must be developed before work commences and must be readily accessible to any worker carrying out the high-risk construction work.

keyRequirements: SWMS required for all 19 categories of high-risk construction work
Work on or near a road, railway, shipping lane or traffic corridor is high-risk
Work involving movement of powered mobile plant is high-risk
SWMS must be prepared before work commences
SWMS must be accessible to workers carrying out the high-risk work
A SWMS is not required for work of a minor nature
